key_insight: IDiom is an autoregressive protein language model for intrinsically disordered regions, and RL-SAE lets designers steer sequence generation by rewarding sparse autoencoder features tied to desired functions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more interpretable and composable route to protein design for disordered regions, which could aid engineered regulation, localization, and signaling in synthetic biology.
method: Trained IDiom on IDiom-DB, a corpus of 54 million predicted IDRs from the AlphaFold Database.
Added RL-SAE post-training to reward activation of specified sparse autoencoder feature sets during generation.
Compared against activation steering and supervised fine-tuning across multiple IDR design tasks.
evidence_signal: Across eight IDR design tasks, RL-SAE sequences activated about 90% of 30 targeted features on average, versus 24% for activation steering, and improved predicted localization and transcriptional activity.
watch_item: Performance is based on predicted features and downstream annotations rather than direct wet-lab validation, so biological success may depend on experimental confirmation.
paper_title: Generative modeling of intrinsically disordered protein regions by reinforcing sparse autoencoder features
